summary.intent: Drive CipherBox v2's wave-6→wave-7 cycle end to end: issue hygiene, audit and fix a live grant-tag security defect (#1135/#1127), plan and launch wave-7 as parallel file-owned batches, consolidate the resulting PRs, and shepherd them through CodeRabbit review to merge — then set up wave 8.
summary.outcome: PR #1141 (grant tag re-mint fix) merged and closed #1135/#1127; wave 7 launched as 8 batches, consolidated to 8 PRs, all merged after CodeRabbit review cycles (with #1170, #1159, #1162, #1163-1169 filed as tracked residuals); branch protection updated with 'Web Engine WASM' as a required context and a stale unused-import warning fixed; wave 8 planning was about to begin when the transcript ends.

repo: crates/engine/src/facade.rs is the dominant hot-file contention point — 7+ issues land on it; #1016's Engine::command signature change forces edits in wasm/host.rs and fuse/ops.rs too.
GitHub sub-issues/dependencies APIs are keyed by database id, not issue number; REST '.parent' is always null — use 'parent_issue_url'.
Writing 'Does not close #NNNN' in a PR body still auto-closes the issue — GitHub's linked-issue parser matches 'close #NNNN' regardless of negation.

CodeRabbit's hourly review-slot window is measured from when a review STARTS, not when its verdict lands; a frozen/stuck run is detectable by the status comment's `updated_at` timestamp never advancing (not by the 'processing' text).
`@coderabbitai review` only covers commits since the last review and is a no-op on an unchanged head; `@coderabbitai full review` forces a fresh pass.
CodeRabbit CLI (v0.7.1) under-reports vs the full web review — proven directly: 0 findings via CLI vs 1 via web on the identical commit.
Branch protection in this repo has strict=false (no forced up-to-date) and a SKIPPED required context satisfies protection (proven by PR #1113 merging with Web Bundle:SKIPPED).
scripts/check-tracker-refs.mjs only scans crates/apps/packages/landing/tools/scripts/.github with code extensions — blueprint/*.md is unscanned, so bare issue numbers there are undetectable drift.
Rebasing a PR's base via GitHub API does NOT trigger a fresh CI run automatically — #1157 sat with only 5/26 required checks after a base retarget until manually rebased.
`git checkout main` fails inside a worktree if main is checked out elsewhere — caused an accidental branch-cut-from-wrong-branch bug during B7.
Windows CI 'link.exe exit code 1104' while linking cipherbox-core's kat_gen example is a known transient flake, distinct from the pre-existing Web E2E Smoke sign-out flake.

Web E2E Smoke has (at least) two independent flaky signatures: sign-out (smoke.spec.ts:44) and front-door login-button visibility (smoke.spec.ts:6) — neither was tracked in an issue until this session (#1169).

Inline Bash-tool commands in this harness run under zsh, which does not word-split unquoted variable expansions — `$GH pr view` or `$R` (multi-word) silently fail as 'command not found'/'unknown flag', producing empty output that can be misread as a failed API call.
husky's pre-commit lint-staged hook fails in a fresh worktree without node_modules — requires --no-verify for Rust-only commits (CI's own Lint/Typecheck/Tracker Refs gates remain the real backstop).

code.finding: reseal_root/remint_grants must run enforce_committed_ledger BEFORE re-minting grant rows and re-derive tags at the OLD name before minting at the new one — ordering is load-bearing to prevent a self-upgraded ledger row landing in an owner-signed commitment.
mint_grant_row takes raw recipient_identity_pk bytes uninterpreted rather than parsing to EcdsaVerifier — parsing it would let an attacker veto their own revocation wave via an unparseable key.
truncate_handle only clears Base::Empty when size==0, so shrink-then-grow resurrects pre-truncate plaintext into the next published version (fixed by adding a base_len truncation floor).
commit() only pushed Invalidation::Attributes after commit_write, never Invalidation::Data, so another open handle could keep serving stale kernel-cached pages after a successful write commit.

HeldRecords is keyed by 16-byte node id and HeldRecord.head_cid is required (empty heads skipped) — scope pointer (has key, no head) and settings record (has head, no key) need complementary shape fixes, not one shared change.

publish_prune calls mark_published immediately on ack, before owe_retires journals the debt — a crash between the two loses the retire debt permanently since dropped roots become unnameable after a shortened history publishes (tracked as #1170).

OpId was imported but only used under #[cfg(test)], causing an unused-import warning on wasm32 builds invisible to any gate (clippy never builds wasm32, wasm check doesn't use -D warnings) — fixed by moving the import into the test module.

workflow: File-ownership batching (disjoint file sets per parallel agent) is more reliable than issue-count batching for avoiding merge conflicts; verify with git merge-tree pairwise AND a cumulative compile check, since MERGEABLE=true on GitHub says nothing about semantic (shape-change) conflicts between two branches.
Never edit a running shell script — bash reads by byte offset, so in-place edits corrupt an executing instance; stop it first (TaskStop), edit, then relaunch.
Never pipe a gate's exit code through `tail`/other commands in zsh — PIPESTATUS isn't populated; redirect to a file and read $? directly.

When resolving a git conflict via append-both, check for shared leading AND trailing context (not just the marked hunk) — git can split a shared preamble or closing braces as 'common', silently truncating one side.
After any git rebase, verify diff SCOPE preservation (file list + line counts) rather than diffing old-tip vs new-tip directly (which necessarily differs by the pulled-in base commits).
A finished background agent's local worktree branch ref can go stale relative to origin — reset --hard to the origin ref before rebasing/continuing work on it.

Follow-up issues filed by subagents consistently arrive orphaned (only a generic label, no parent/component/milestone/edges) — this needed fixing after nearly every batch; worth baking into agent briefs as a hard requirement.
Consolidating multiple small same-subsystem PRs into one both reduces reviewer slot pressure and can eliminate real merge conflicts between the consolidated PRs themselves.
Distinguish CI flakes from real regressions by comparing the identical check against the PR's own prior head or sibling PRs from the same session, rather than assuming either flake or regression.

Health-gate any scripted GitHub-API-dependent flow (require N consecutive successful probes) before flipping a PR ready — a mid-flip failure during an API outage can leave a PR ready-and-unattended, silently burning or missing a review slot.

friction: CodeRabbit web reviews stalled/froze indefinitely on #1151 (status comment updated_at frozen for 65+ minutes with no verdict), wasting most of an hourly slot before being diagnosed and worked around via the CLI plus a forced full review.
GitHub API had a full outage (0/10 REST, 0/5 GraphQL probes) mid-session, aborting a scheduled review flip.

Own scripting bugs repeatedly cost time: no retry on transient empty head-reads (false 'HEAD MOVED' abort), MINCHECKS mis-tuned per PR causing early or late flips, misdiagnosed root cause for background-shell gh failures (wrongly blamed cwd/--repo when it was actually zsh word-splitting on unquoted multi-word variables), and a parser keying on CodeRabbit's 'Actionable comments posted' header which is omitted entirely when count is zero (caused an unnecessary re-draft of a clean PR).
Retargeting a PR's base via API silently does not trigger CI re-run, leaving it missing 21 required checks undetected until manually caught.
Macroscope reviewer out of credits for the entire session (skipped on every PR); Greptile inactive/not reviewing despite believed to have no cap.
A review sub-agent ran `git checkout --` on the working tree and destroyed 3 in-flight edits, mistaking concurrent work for a rogue process.
Auto-close via ambiguous negated closing keyword ('Does not close #1016') silently closed a wrong issue and its downstream unblocking effects.

User had to directly point out several planning/accounting misses: 11 PRs when only 6 batches were promised, wrong slot-time arithmetic (computed from verdict landing rather than review start), untracked blueprint residual that should have been a GitHub issue.

#856 — needs an account-namespacing FloorStore decorator across ~10 facade.rs call sites; scheduled to run only once facade.rs work (#1016) is free.
